key_insight: Proximity to a metal-insulator transition can be used to tune correlated-oxide transparent conductors so they become more transparent without completely sacrificing metallic transport.
engineering_relevance: This provides a materials-design rule for optimizing transparent electrodes in optoelectronic and silicon-photovoltaic devices by adjusting electronic filling near the MIT.
method: Use epitaxial Ti-substituted SrVO3 films as a model correlated-oxide transparent conductor.
Systematically vary composition to move toward the metal-insulator transition and track optical window and conductivity together.
Assess performance with Haacke figure-of-merit analysis and spectral-weight measurements near the Fermi level.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic widening of the optical window into silicon-photovoltaic-relevant ranges, with optimal figures of merit found near the composition-driven MIT despite reduced coherent transport.
watch_item: Near the optimal regime, disorder and carrier depletion can erode coherent conductivity, so implementation must balance transparency gains against transport loss.
paper_title: Engineering Correlated Transparent Conductors via Metal-Insulator Transition Proximity
